The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this Request for Quotation (RFQ) to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the RFQ and represents the overall Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government, price and other factors considered. LPTA is determined by evaluating all non-cost proposals on an "acceptable vs. unacceptable" basis. Once a quotation meets the minimum objective standards deﬁned in the solicitation, the contract is awarded to the offeror with the lowest evaluated price, with no additional value given for exceeding technical requirements. To be eligible for award, the offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at SAM.gov, have current representations and certiﬁcations, and not be listed on the SAM exclusions list. The Government will review each offeror's price and order them from lowest to highest priced. The Government will evaluate quotations in ascending price order until a minimum of two (2) quotations are determined to be Technically Acceptable. Under the LPTA approach, the Government will evaluate the three (3) lowest quotes up front if more than 3 offerors are received. This source selection will evaluate the lowest-price quote ﬁrst for technical acceptability, if it passes, the award will be made;

Effective air circulation in flight line facilities is critical for personnel safety, aircraft performance, and overall mission success. Since installation five years ago, the fans have not been serviced, increasing the risk of mechanical failure. An

n Antonio, Randolph Air Force Base (JBSA-Randolph) aircraft hangars. Effective air circulation in flight line facilities is critical for personnel safety, aircraft performance, and overall mission success. Since installation five years ago, the fans have not been serviced, increasing the risk of mechanical failure. An inoperable fan system poses a significant threat to both personnel (heat-related injuries) and sensitive aircraft components. This contract proactively maintains the integrity and safety of these vital hangar environments and mitigates the risks associated with equipment failure. 1.0 SCOPE. This PWS defines the requirements for a non-personal services to provide maintenance, repair, and installation at JBSA-Randolph. The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, materials, parts, transportation, and equipment (including all necessary lift equipment) to replace inoperable existing fans, perform annual preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and optional repairs for twenty-one (21) fans located across five (5) buildings. 1.1 Non-Personal Services. The Contractor shall perform annual preventive maintenance (PM) on all twenty-one (21) fans during each period of performance. To ensure standardized annual intervals, the Contractor shall execute the required PM event no earlier than four (4) months and no later than seven (7) months into the period of performance. forms_signatures.text: . 1.0 SCOPE. This PWS defines the requirements for a non-personal services to provide maintenance, repair, and installation at JBSA-Randolph. The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, materials, parts, transportation, and equipment (including all necessary lift equipment) to replace inoperable existing fans, perform annual preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and optional repairs for twenty-one (21) fans located across five (5) buildings. 1.1 Non-Personal Services. The government will neither supervise contractor employees, nor control the methods the contractor performs the required tasks, nor prepare work schedules for individual contractor employees; however, the contractor shall consider the Government’s duty hours and work schedule. If the contractor feels that any actions constitute or are perceived to constitute personal services, the contractor shall notify the Contractor Officer (CO) immediately. 2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS. The contractor shall comply with the following documents and standards in the performance of this contract: • Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Maintenance and Safety Manuals • National Electrical Code (NEC) Standards • Air Force Occupational Safety and Health (AFOSH) Standards • National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Standards • Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) and applicable ETL fire safety standards 3.0 REQUIREMENT 3.1 Annual Preventative Maintenance. The Contractor shall perform annual preventive maintenance (PM) on all twenty-one (21) fans during each period of performance. To ensure standardized annual intervals, the Contractor shall execute the required PM event no earlier than four (4) months and no later than seven (7) months into the period of performance. The aptitudes and abilities measured by the ASVAB include General Science, Arithmetic Reasoning, Word Knowledge, Paragraph Comprehension, Mathematics Knowledge, Electronics Information, Auto Information, Shop Information, Mechanical Comprehension, and Assembling Objects. Test takers receive a standardized score from 1-100 for each of these subtests. The Army combines scores on the ASVAB subtests into composites, also known as aptitude areas (AAs) or line scores, to determine eligibility into each initial-entry MOS. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. There are currently 10 AA composites that are used to determine MOS eligibility: Clerical, Combat, Electronics, Field Artillery, General Maintenance, General Technical, Mechanical Maintenance, Operators and Food, Surveillance and Communications, and Skilled Technical. The Army combines scores on the ASVAB subtests into composites, also known as aptitude areas (AAs) or line scores, to determine eligibility into each initial-entry MOS. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. There are currently 10 AA composites that are used to determine MOS eligibility: Clerical, Combat, Electronics, Field Artillery, General Maintenance, General Technical, Mechanical Maintenance, Operators and Food, Surveillance and Communications, and Skilled Technical. Effective classification and assignment of Soldiers is dependent on being able to discriminate the different abilities of Soldiers based on how well they score on the AA composites of the ASVAB. The overarching objective of this effort is to conduct research to determine if the Army would benefit from updated AA composites used to determine MOS fit. The current project aims to identify potential redundancy within the current ASVAB AA composites,

The multi-domain operations (MDO) concept requires Army teams to operate semi-independently but also to utilize the capabilities across multiple domains to conduct sustained missions in highly contested environments. Additionally, high personnel turnover for teams is expected in the FOE as casualty counts increase, rapid teaming is required, and ad hoc teams become common. Within the literature, creativity has been conceptualized and examined as both an antecedent (e.g., Yang & Hung, 2021; Zhang & Bartol, 2010) and an outcome (e.g., Liu et al., 2022; Tierney & Farmer, 2011). In a recent review by Lua et al. (2024), the authors discuss creativity behaviors like idea implementation, innovative behavior, and personal initiative. Teng et al. (2020) examined the relationship between creative self-efficacy and innovative behavior. In the study, the authors used Scott and Bruce’s (1994) measure of innovative behaviors which includes items such as “generates creative ideas” and “develops adequate plans and schedules for the implementation of new ideas” (p. 607). For the purpose of this effort, we are interested in creativity as an outcome and, more specifically, creative performance with technology. Creativity research is not novel to the U.S. Army, but largely exists at the antecedent level. Two previous job analysis projects included innovation and creativity in surveys of talent requirements (Boyle et al., 2022) and personnel characteristics (Royston & Lin, 2022) across military occupational specialties (MOS). Additional ARI efforts have examined divergent thinking (Russell et al., 2017) and creative thinking (Zaccaro et al., 2012). Results for these reports indicate the importance of creativity across MOS and ranks but are not specific to creative performance behaviors with technology. 4 The purpose of this project is to develop and validate a measure of creative performance with technology. Measure items should capture individual-level indicators of creative performance that are relevant for Soldiers. This measure may capture a single domain or may involve multiple subscales. WHITE PAPER TOPIC: Refinement of the Common Cyber Capabilities Assessment A promising strategy to meet the increasing Cyber personnel demands is to select entry-level staff with little or no formal information technology education, but high potential, and then make investments in training. One means to identify high-potential candidates for training is to build a measure of the skills and abilities most typically associated with success across the military Cyber jobs. Cyber training for enlisted Soldiers is lengthy, challenging, and requires significant investment from the Army. The necessity of Cyber jobs has led to an increasing demand for quality personnel. By assessing the underlying skills and abilities associated with success in Cyber work, the Army can identify high- potential candidates, meet the increasing demand for these personnel, more accurately predict performance, and reduce attrition during the training process. To aid in identification of high-potential candidates for Cyber training, the Army Research Institute (ARI) developed the Common Cyber Capabilities assessment (C^3).

When required to maintain access to required IT systems or networks, the contractor shall ensure that all contractor employees requiring access complete annual Cyber Awareness training, and maintain a current requisite background investigation. The Contractor's Security Representative shall contact the Command Security Manager for guidance when reinvestigations are required. UNICACIÓNLos licitadores deberán tener en cuenta, a la hora de configurar su oferta, todos los servicios requeridos en este Anexo para la impartición de las acciones formativas, de comunicación y gestión del cambio necesarias, asegurando el correcto traspaso del conocimiento y la divulgación de cada evolutivo planificado.NORMATIVACon relación a la formación que pudiera llevarse a cabo durante la vigencia del contrato, se atendrá a las directrices establecidas por la Dirección competente en esta materia en Madrid Digital. A este respecto, indicar que la dirección competente ha de regirse por un Sistema de Gestión de Calidad basado en la norma ISO 9000-2015, tal y como establece su Convenio Colectivo y que, naturalmente, se audita. Las actividades realizadas y el cumplimiento de la normativa descrita serán validados por la Dirección competente de la Agencia en materia de formación, comunicación y gestión del cambio.DEFINICIÓN DEL PLAN DE FORMACIÓNEl adjudicatario desarrollará un Plan de Formación atendiendo a los hitos establecidos en el Plan de Proyecto o en la ejecución de cualquiera de los servicios objeto del pliego, y deberá ser presentado a la Agencia con laantelación suficiente para que esté validado antes de que se inicie la fase de implantación. El Plan de Formación deberá inclui

vas.iv.Ámbito y Perfiles de Formación, distinguiendo entre:Usuarios de la Comunidad de Madrid, con sus diferentes perfilesEmpleados de la Agencia, con sus diferentes perfiles (mantenimiento legal, correctivo y evolutivo, soporte y atención a los usuarios, formadores, etc.)La formación se llevará a cabo, preferentemente en las instalaciones de la Agencia. No obstante, el adjudicatario tendrá que tener disponibilidad de las instalaciones que sean necesarias para el desarrollo de las acciones formativas planificadas, si así se lo requiere la Agencia.Dichas instalaciones deberán cumplir con la normativa relativa al Sistema de Gestión de Calidad (ISO 9001:2008),y así mismo, deberán estar ubicadas en una zona céntrica y bien comunicada de Madrid. Las instalaciones propuestas deberán tener todos los elementos necesarios para la impartición de las acciones formativas (fundamentalmente en lo que atañe a los equipos informáticos, instalaciones y mobiliario, accesibilidad y aspectos básicos de seguridad). Así mismo, si hiciese falta alguna conexión a las infraestructuras de la Agencia, éstas correrán a cargo del adjudicatario. La validación definitiva de las aulas, lahará la Agencia, de acuerdo con el estándar establecido.La formación dirigida a los diferentes perfiles deberá impartirse con el grad

umple con los objetivos de continuidad de negocio definidos en el proyecto Nexus.Transparencia para el usuario: Cambio entre CPDs sin interrupciones perceptibles.Gracias a la replicación activa y a los mecanismos de conmutación automática (failover), el traspaso de operaciones entre CPDs se realiza de forma imperceptible para los usuarios. Esto garantiza una Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 261 de 329 experiencia fluida y sin degradación del rendimiento, incluso durante eventos críticos o mantenimientos programados.Seguridad reforzada: Cumplimiento de estándares internacionales.El Geocluster incorpora prácticas alineadas con normativas como ISO 27001 y NIST, asegurando la protección de datos y la resiliencia ante ciberataques. La redundancia y la sincronización constante contribuyen a minimizar riesgos asociados a pérdida de información o accesos no autorizados.Flexibilidad operativa: Mantenimientos sin impacto en la carga productiva.Al contar con servidores activos en más de un CPD, es posible realizar intervenciones técnicas, actualizaciones o pruebas en uno de los centros sin afectar la operación global. Esto optimiza la gestión de recursos, reduce ventanas de mantenimiento y mejora la eficiencia del equipo técnico.*** FIN DEL ANEXO 7 *** Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 262 de 329 ANE

Factores operativos Continuidad del servicio: mantener la solución tecnológica basada en SAP garantiza el mantenimiento y evolución de este servicio público esencial que afecta a la gestión de ingresos, pagos, presupuesto, contabilidad, compras, logística y contratación de toda la Comunidad de Madrid. lizada a través de la Oficina de Proyecto y Producto, estructurada en torno a buenas prácticas SAP. Factores económicos Maximización de la inversión pública realizada durante más de 15 años en licencias, parametrización, desarrollos, integraciones y formación. Aprovechamiento de licencias y suscripciones adquiridas, cuyo coste ya ha sido asumido en expedientes recientes. Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026 Página 5 de 12 Evitar un coste muy elevado de sustitución, dado que cambiar de plataforma obligaría a reimplantar desde cero todos los procesos, suponiendo además incurrir en costes redundantes por duplicación de sistemas de gran complejidad y volumetría de gestión Prevención de sobrecostes normativos , ya que SAP incorpora actualizaciones estándar alineadas con normativa de contabilidad y contratación. La continuidad de NEXUS ECCL sobre tecnología SAP es la opción más eficiente, segura, sostenible y alineada con las inversiones realizadas y los requisitos del servicio público. Un cambio tecnológico supondría riesgos y sobrecostes injustificables, comprometiendo la operativa económico-financiera de la Comunidad de Madrid.
